Dear Ms. Botes,

​I acknowledge your email of 10 April 2026 (15:40).

​While I note your statement that Inlexso acts solely as a transcription
service, I must clarify that under South African law, a service provider
contracted by the Office of the Chief Justice (OCJ) to manage the Primary
Record of court proceedings acts as an administrative extension of the
court.

​You are included in this correspondence because:

​Your office was placed on formal notice of the urgency of this request on
26 March 2026. The subsequent seven-day administrative vacuum—caused by
your absence and the lack of a formal handover to your colleague, Tina—has
directly prejudiced my ability to file a Rule 42 Rescission.

​As the custodian of the audio from 25 March 2026 (specifically
14:05–14:23), Inlexso is now formally on notice that this recording
contains evidence of judicial conduct and procedural irregularities. Any
failure to preserve or provide this record will be cited in my report to
the Judicial Conduct Tribunal.

​The demand for a 50% deposit (Quote BB08042601) from a litigant in a
documented state of destitution constitutes a financial barrier to a
Constitutional right (Section 34).

​I am not asking you to act as an "advocate." I am placing on record that
Inlexso is holding a public record behind a commercial paywall while the
court administration remains silent.

​I require a formal confirmation by close of business that the audio files
have been preserved and that you have sought a fee-waiver instruction from
the Acting Chief Registrar (Ms. Hanekom) in light of the documented medical
and financial duress in this matter.

​Sincerely,
Wilbur William Matthee

> Dear Honorable Members and Directors,
>
> ​Please find the attached Comprehensive Memorandum (Ref: EH/JO/2026/001)
> regarding a sustained and systemic obstruction of justice currently being
> perpetrated by officials within the Office of the Chief Justice (OCJ).
>
> ​As a whistleblower in a state of government-acknowledged destitution and
> homelessness, I am submitting this formal indictment to record the
> following critical failures:
>
> ​Administrative Attrition: A 28-day delay by the Labour Court in March
> 2026 which forced me into the High Court under extreme medical and
> financial duress.
>
> ​Procedural Persecution: A High Court hearing (Case No: 2026-066952) where
> my disclosed PTSD was mocked by the Bench, and where I was "represented" by
> an unauthorized Advocate who was committed for 72-hour psychiatric
> observation immediately following the hearing.
>
> ​Concealment of Evidence: The intentional withholding of court audio
> recordings since 26 March 2026, which capture the mockery and procedural
> collapse mentioned above, effectively blocking my right to a Rule 42
> Rescission.
>
> ​Material Misrepresentation & Data Breach: The active falsification of
> court records today, 10 April 2026, to mask a statutory filing deadline
> failure, alongside a gross POPIA breach involving the disclosure of a third
> party’s (Armstrong vs. City of Cape Town) confidential legal documents.
>
> ​The attached memorandum details how these actions constitute a
> "functional denial of justice" and a direct violation of Section 34 of the
> Constitution.
>
> ​I am a citizen seeking the protection of the Law; instead, I have been
> met with administrative trickery and the weaponization of my poverty. I
> request the Committee’s urgent intervention and a Judicial Directive to
> rectify these records and preserve my statutory rights.
>
> ​Respectfully,
>
> Wilbur William Matthee
